newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rundle twins get Stuart green light.
newsitem.headline: Rundle twins get Stuart green light.

text.p: Shale oil hopefuls Central Pacific Minerals and Southern Pacific Petroleum NL, commonly known as the Rundle Twins, announced on Wednesday they had agreed with financiers to proceed with the stage one development of the Stuart shale oil deposit.

The companies said they had completed discussions with the Queensland government over the High Court's Wik judgment and were satisfied with all aspects of the mining lease covering the Stuart project. The two companies had also agreed to a state government infrastructure assistance package.
The Stuart Shale project is being developed jointly between the Rundle Twins and Canada's Suncor Inc.
The Rundle Twins said they had secured overall funding commitment to stage one for up to $114 million, a portion of which may be advanced by them in the form of a project finance loan.
When met, these commitments would result in the Rundle twins receiving a total of 50 percent of the stage one project cashflow by way of return of equity and project financing loan repayment.

Stuart stage one is the first of three planned stages to develop the oil shale deposit and involves construction of a plant to produce 4,500 barrels of oil per day at an estimated cost of A$250 million.
The companies said subsequent stages could raise production progressively to a total of 95,000 barrels per day with the prospect of additional production thereafter.
